thm:optimization-preserving-compiler.proof_tex:
Fix \(i\in[H]\) and \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\).  The sign is fixed throughout and is not an eliminated variable.

For \(x\ne x_t\), define
\[
 u_{t,x}(y)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac{K_t(y\mid x)}{p_t}\right\},
 \qquad y\in\mathcal S.
 \tag{1}
\]
The division is valid by \(\texttt{ass:factual-positivity}\).  By \(\texttt{def:posterior-row-fiber}\), the feasible factor for this row is the capped simplex
\[
 \mathcal P_{t,x}=
 \left\{v\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal S}:0\le v(y)\le u_{t,x}(y),\ 
              \sum_{y\in\mathcal S}v(y)=1\right\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
It is nonempty.  Indeed, \(\sum_yK_t(y\mid x)/p_t=1/p_t\ge1\).  If one untruncated cap is at least one, then the sum of the truncated caps is at least one; otherwise truncation changes no cap.  Thus \(\sum_yu_{t,x}(y)\ge1\), and mass one can be filled beneath the caps.  The factual-row factor is the singleton \(\{\delta_{y_t}\}\).

A point of \(\mathcal P_{t,x}\) is a vertex if and only if all but at most one coordinate are at either zero or their upper cap.  If two coordinates are strictly between their bounds, a sufficiently small transfer of mass between them gives two distinct feasible points with the original point as midpoint.  Conversely, in a convex decomposition of a point with all but at most one coordinate at a bound, every bound coordinate agrees in the two summands, and the sum-to-one constraint fixes the remaining coordinate.

These vertices can be listed exactly in output-sensitive time.  Start from the vertex obtained by filling coordinates in a fixed order to their caps until the residual mass fits in one coordinate.  From a listed vertex, test every ordered transfer direction \(e_y-e_{y'}\) that is locally feasible, move maximally in that direction, and retain the endpoint if it has the vertex form just proved.  These moves traverse every edge because an edge of the box intersected with the sum hyperplane can free at most two box constraints.  To verify reachability, fix any target vertex \(v^\star\).  Assign coefficient one to coordinates at their upper cap in \(v^\star\), coefficient minus one to coordinates that are zero there, and coefficient zero to its possible unique non-bound coordinate.  The resulting linear functional is uniquely maximized at \(v^\star\).  At any other vertex, \(v^\star-v\) decomposes into transfers from decreasing to increasing coordinates; when \(v\) has a unique non-bound coordinate, a transfer between two bound coordinates can be split through that coordinate.  At least one locally feasible transfer strictly increases the functional.  Maximal movement reaches another vertex, and finiteness forces a path to \(v^\star\).  Hence breadth-first traversal with duplicate suppression lists all vertices in \(O(|\mathcal S|^2v_{t,x})\) rational operations when this row has \(v_{t,x}\) vertices.  Every listed coordinate is zero, a cap, or one minus a sum of caps, so its bit length is polynomial in the rational input length.

Let \(Z_{t,x}\) select one listed vertex \(q^Z_{t,x}\), using a one-point alphabet for a singleton row.  The vertex-witness assertion of \(\texttt{thm:sharp-shared-interval}\), together with \(\texttt{prop:affine-nonnegative-lift}\), gives
\[
 V_\sigma=\max_z F_i^\sigma(q^z),
 \tag{3}
\]
where \(z\) is one joint assignment of every row selector.  Thus this finite outer maximization already imposes one row assignment shared by all coalition worlds.

We now construct the nonnegative circuit.  Exact quadrature applied to the constant polynomial gives \(\sum_{j=1}^H\nu_j=1\), whence \(C_\nu=\sum_j|\nu_j|\ge1\).  Put
\[
 \rho_{jb}=\frac{|a_{jb}^\sigma|}{2C_\nu},
 \qquad
 \eta_{jb}=\begin{cases}+,&a_{jb}^\sigma\ge0,\\-,&a_{jb}^\sigma<0.\end{cases}
 \tag{4}
\]
Because \(|a_{j0}^\sigma|=|a_{j1}^\sigma|=|\nu_j|\), \(\sum_{j,b}\rho_{jb}=1\).  Introduce one global chance variable \(W\) with alphabet \([H]\times\{0,1\}\times[H]\) and law
\[
 \Pr\{W=(j,b,\ell)\}=\frac{\rho_{jb}}{H}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Conditional on its first two coordinates, use at time \(t\) the action kernel
\[
 \gamma_t^{jb}(a\mid s)=
 \begin{cases}
  \alpha_i^b(a\mid s),&t=i,\\
  (1-\zeta_j)\alpha_t^0(a\mid s)+\zeta_j\alpha_t^1(a\mid s),&t\ne i.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{6}
\]
For each row insert
\[
 \psi_{t,x}(S_t,A_t,S_{t+1},Z_{t,x})=
 \begin{cases}
 q^{Z}_{t,x}(S_{t+1}),&(S_t,A_t)=x,\\
 1,&(S_t,A_t)\ne x,
 \end{cases}
 \tag{7}
\]
and insert the initial factor \(\mathbf 1\{S_1=s_1\}\).  Finally insert, for every reward time,
\[
 \chi_t(W,S_t,A_t,S_{t+1})=
 \begin{cases}
 Hh_t^{\eta_{jb}}((S_t,A_t),S_{t+1}),&W=(j,b,t),\\
 1,&W=(j,b,\ell),\ \ell\ne t.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{8}
\]
All factors are rational and nonnegative.  Rationality follows from the theorem's input restrictions and the rational vertex construction.  Nonnegativity follows from \(R>0\), the definitions of \(m_t,M_t\), and \(\texttt{prop:affine-nonnegative-lift}\).  Equation (7) contains exactly one variable \(Z_{t,x}\) for each row; no copy is created when \(W\), the state path, or the selected reward time changes.

Fix \(z\) and sum the product of (5)--(8), the policy factors, and the initial factor over \(W\), all actions, and \(S_2,\ldots,S_{H+1}\).  For a realized \((S_t,A_t)\), the product of (7) over \(x\in\mathcal X\) is exactly \(q^z_{t,(S_t,A_t)}(S_{t+1})\).  Hence the path sum is a Markov expectation under the single kernel \(q^z\).  Averaging first over the reward-time coordinate and then over \((j,b)\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 T_\sigma(z)
 &=\sum_{j=1}^H\sum_{b=0}^1\rho_{jb}
   \mathbb E_{q^z}\!\left[
    \sum_{t=1}^H h_t^{\eta_{jb}}((S_t,A_t),S_{t+1})
    \mathrel{\big|}S_1=s_1,\gamma^{jb}\right]\\
 &=\frac{1}{2C_\nu}F_i^\sigma(q^z).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{9}
\]
For positive sign in (4), the expectation is \(h_{jb}(q^z)\) by \(\texttt{def:nonnegative-endpoint-objectives}\).  For negative sign, the pathwise complementary-leaf identity in \(\texttt{prop:affine-nonnegative-lift}\) makes it \(1-h_{jb}(q^z)\).  Thus the circuit followed by deterministic multiplication by \(2C_\nu\) realizes \(F_i^\sigma\) exactly.  This is \(\mathfrak F_i^\sigma\) from \(\texttt{def:compiler-handle}\).

We next prove optimization preservation.  Bucket elimination maintains nonnegative factors.  Summing a chance variable is exact by distributivity because factors outside its bucket do not contain it.  Suppose a decision variable \(Z\) is next maximized.  Multiply the current factors containing \(Z\) into \(A(Z,Y)\), where \(Y\) consists of the other uneliminated decisions in that bucket.  Legality of \(\preceq\) implies that no uneliminated chance variable occurs in \(A\).  The product of all factors outside the bucket can be written \(B(X,Y,Y')\), where \(X\) are remaining chance variables, \(Y'\) are other decisions, and \(B\) does not contain \(Z\).  Pointwise, nonnegativity gives
\[
 \max_Z\{A(Z,Y)B(X,Y,Y')\}
 =B(X,Y,Y')\max_ZA(Z,Y).
 \tag{10}
\]
Thus this maximization commutes outward past every still-unperformed chance summation; its choice may depend on later decisions but not on a chance realization.  Finite maxima over decisions commute with one another.  Induction over buckets, using distributivity at chance buckets and (10) at decision buckets, reduces the returned value to
\[
 2C_\nu\max_z\sum_{W,S_2,\ldots,S_{H+1},A_1,\ldots,A_H}
       \mathfrak F_i^\sigma(z,W,S,A)
 =\max_zF_i^\sigma(q^z)=V_\sigma,
 \tag{11}
\]
where (9) and (3) give the two equalities.  This proves the mixed-elimination invariant while retaining one outer row assignment.

For the operation count, a bucket contains at most \(w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)+1\) nonglobal live variables, each with alphabet at most \(d\).  The one global variable \(W\) has \(2H^2\) values.  Therefore every bucket table has at most
\[
 2H^2d^{w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)+1}
 \tag{12}
\]
entries, with the same expression an upper bound when \(W\) is absent.  Multiplication and elimination use a constant number of rational operations per table entry per consumed factor.  Each initial factor is consumed once, and each eliminated variable creates at most one factor that is later consumed once.  Since \(N\) bounds variables plus initial factors, summing bucket-factor incidences gives
\[
 O\!\left(H^2N d^{w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)+1}\right)
 \tag{13}
\]
rational operations.  Vertex listing costs \(O(N|\mathcal S|^2d)\).  If a non-singleton selector exists, its transition factor contains that selector, current state, action, and next state, so the width term in (13), with \(|\mathcal S|\le d\), absorbs this preprocessing; if every row is a singleton, no nontrivial listing is needed.  The remaining factor construction is also absorbed by (13).

Let \(B_0\) be the binary length of the rational input.  Every cap in (1), every vertex coordinate, and every initial factor entry has bit length polynomial in \(B_0\).  For a fixed remaining decision context, an intermediate entry expands into a sum of products of primitive factor entries, with each primitive factor used at most once in a product.  A common product of their denominators has bit length \(O(NB_0)\).  There are at most \((2H^2)d^N\) chance assignments, adding only \(O(\log H+N\log d)\) numerator bits.  Maximization selects one candidate rational and introduces no new denominator.  A capped simplex has at most \(|\mathcal S|2^{|\mathcal S|-1}\) vertices by the proved vertex characterization, so \(\log d\) is itself bounded by a polynomial in the explicit input length.  Reduced intermediate and exact output rationals therefore have bit length polynomial in \(B_0\) and \(N\); reporting a requested binary approximation adds only the requested output precision.

At each maximization bucket, store a maximizing selector value for every assignment of the later decision variables in its output scope, breaking ties deterministically.  Reverse-order backtracking fixes those later variables before consulting the stored value.  Legality removed every chance variable from a maximization bucket, so no stored choice depends on \(W\), a state, or an action realization.  Hence \(\mathsf{BP}_\sigma\) recovers one joint row assignment \(z_\sigma\), shared by all quadrature branches and all paths.

It remains to construct the endpoint SCM compactly.  At time \(t\), draw \(E_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_t)\).  Conditional on \(E_t=1\), set the factual coordinate of \(R_t\) to \(y_t\) and draw each nonfactual coordinate from \(q^{z_\sigma}_{t,x}\).  If \(p_t<1\), conditional on \(E_t=0\), draw the factual coordinate from
\[
 \frac{K_t(y\mid x_t)-p_t\mathbf 1\{y=y_t\}}{1-p_t}
 \tag{14}
\]
and each nonfactual coordinate \(x\ne x_t\) from
\[
 \frac{K_t(y\mid x)-p_tq^{z_\sigma}_{t,x}(y)}{1-p_t}.
 \tag{15}
\]
The numerators are nonnegative by membership in \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\), and each distribution sums to one.  The factual residual assigns zero mass to \(y_t\), so conditioning on the factual event forces \(E_t=1\) and induces exactly the selected posterior rows.  Mixing the branches recovers marginal \(K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) for every row.  If \(p_t=1\), the residual branch is absent, and the coordinatewise inequalities together with equality of total mass force \(q^{z_\sigma}_{t,x}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) for every nonfactual row.  Sampling these response tables independently over \(t\) gives the structural equations, transition marginals, and timewise disturbance independence required by \(\mathfrak M(K)\), in agreement with \(\texttt{lem:posterior-row-projection}\).  Equations (14)--(15) specify a conditional sampler rather than an exponential response-table mass array.

Finally, run (11) separately for \(\sigma=+1\) and \(\sigma=-1\).  By \(\texttt{prop:affine-nonnegative-lift}\),
\[
 U_i(K,\tau)=R(V_{+1}-C_\nu),
 \qquad
 L_i(K,\tau)=R(C_\nu-V_{-1}).
\]
The corresponding backtracked SCMs attain the two endpoints and use one shared joint row assignment in every coalition world.  This proves all assertions.

assumptions.ass:factual-action-positivity: For every \(t\in[H]\), the factual-policy cell satisfies \(\pi_t(a_t\mid s_t)>0\).
assumptions.ass:factual-policy-exogeneity: On a finite product extension of the transition probability space, the complete family \(\{V_t:t\in[H]\}\cup\{V_t^C:t\in[H],\ C\subseteq[H]\}\) is mutually independent and jointly independent of \((S_1,U_1,\ldots,U_H)\), with each \(V_t\in\mathcal A^{\mathcal S}\) satisfying \(\Pr\{V_t(s)=a\}=\pi_t(a\mid s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\) and entering the factual equation \(A_t=G_t(S_t,V_t)=V_t(S_t)\), and with each \(V_t^C\in\mathcal A^{\mathcal S}\) satisfying \(\Pr\{V_t^C(s)=a\}=\alpha_t^C(a\mid s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\) and generating the state-contingent action sample \(A_t=V_t^C(S_t)\) in coalition world \(C\).
assumptions.ass:fixed-initial-state: The initial state is fixed: \(S_1=s_1\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:markov-structural-equations: The environment transition equation at time \(t\) is \(S_{t+1}=F_t(S_t,A_t,U_t)\).
assumptions.ass:transition-marginals: For every \(t\in[H]\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(y\in\mathcal S\), \(\Pr\{F_t(x,U_t)=y\}=K_t(y\mid x)\).

thm:quantitative-gap-neighborhood.proof_tex:
At \(\theta^\star\), every factual transition probability is \(1/2\).  A binary nonfactual posterior success probability \(a\) is constrained only by \(a\in[0,1]\), so the fiber coordinates \(u,w,z,v\) range independently over \([0,1]\), while the factual rows are \(\delta_0\).

Put \(\eta=1/64\), \(\beta=63/64\), and \(\epsilon=1/4\).  The fixed initial state, external action coins, and deterministic terminal reward give the direct recursions
\[
 g_\varnothing=0,
 \qquad g_{\{1\}}=\epsilon u\{(1-\eta)z+\eta v\},
 \qquad g_{\{2\}}=\beta w,
\]
and
\[
 g_{\{1,2\}}=(1-\epsilon u)\beta w
 +\epsilon u\{(1-\beta)z+\beta v\}. \tag{1}
\]
For \(H=2\), both Shapley weights are \(1/2\), and \(\beta+\eta=1\).  Therefore
\[
 \Phi_1(q)=\frac{\epsilon u}{2}
 \left[\beta w-\{2-\beta-\eta\}z-(\beta+\eta)v\right]
 =\frac{u}{8}\left(\frac{63}{64}w-z-v\right). \tag{2}
\]
Its minimum is \(-1/4\), attained at \((u,w,z,v)=(1,0,1,1)\), and its maximum is \(63/512\), attained at \((1,1,0,0)\).  By the shared-endpoint definition and the repaired projection theorem, these are compatible-SCM endpoints with independent policy coins.

The separate coalition extrema from (1) are
\[
 \inf g_\varnothing=\sup g_\varnothing=0,
 \quad \inf g_{\{1\}}=0,
 \quad \sup g_{\{1\}}=\frac14,
 \quad \inf g_{\{2\}}=0,
 \quad \sup g_{\{2\}}=\frac{63}{64}.
\]
Also \(\inf g_{\{1,2\}}=0\), and setting all four row coordinates equal to one gives
\[
 \sup g_{\{1,2\}}=\beta+\epsilon(1-\beta)=\frac{253}{256}.
\]
The formula in \(\texttt{def:independent-coalition-outer-bound}\) consequently yields
\[
 \inf\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}=-\frac12\left(\frac14+\frac{253}{256}\right)
 =-\frac{317}{512},
 \qquad
 \sup\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}=\frac12\frac{63}{64}=\frac{63}{128}.
\]
Both excess widths are \(189/512\).

Now fix \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\), where \(\rho=1/1024\) and \(\kappa=511/1024\).  The metric definition gives
\[
 \delta(K,K^\star)<\rho,
 \qquad K_t(0\mid(0,0))>\frac12-\rho=\kappa. \tag{3}
\]
With center rewards and policies held fixed, complete returns lie in \([0,1]\).  The local modulus with \(H=2\) moves either shared endpoint by at most \(8\rho/\kappa\) when \(K^\star\) is replaced by \(K\).

Next hold \(K\), and hence its posterior fiber, fixed while changing rewards and policies.  For any coalition, maximally couple each external action draw.  The rowwise policy \(\ell^1\) discrepancies are below \(\rho\), so each action mismatch probability is below \(\rho/2\); a union bound over two actions gives path-law total variation below \(\rho\).  For fixed paths the two rewards differ by less than \(2\rho\).  Comparing first rewards on a common path and then center rewards across the coupled paths gives, uniformly in feasible \(q\),
\[
 |g_C(q;\theta)-g_C(q;K,r^\star,\pi^\star,\pi_{\mathrm{base}}^\star)|<3\rho. \tag{4}
\]
Because Shapley weights sum to one and every contribution is a difference of two returns, (4) moves \(\Phi_1\), and hence either shared extremum over the unchanged fiber, by less than \(6\rho\).  Thus each shared endpoint moves from its center value by at most
\[
 A=\frac{8\rho}{\kappa}+6\rho. \tag{5}
\]

The same \(A\) bounds either endpoint of the internal relaxation.  Indeed, the row-matching construction in the proof of \(\texttt{thm:local-positivity-modulus}\), applied between \(K^\star\) and \(K\), moves each posterior row by total variation below \(2\rho/\kappa\).  Sequential coupling over two transitions moves an extremum of any center-reward coalition return by at most \(4\rho/\kappa\); equation (4) adds \(3\rho\).  An endpoint of the internal interval has total absolute coefficient two, giving the bound \(2(4\rho/\kappa+3\rho)=A\).  Consequently
\[
 \min\{\Delta_1^-(\theta),\Delta_1^+(\theta)\}
 \ge\frac{189}{512}-2A
 =\frac{183}{512}-\frac{16}{511}>\frac14, \tag{6}
\]
where the last inequality is equivalent to \(55\cdot511>16\cdot512\).

The remaining certificates follow directly from the metric ball.  Coordinate differences are bounded by rowwise \(\ell^1\) differences, so
\[
 \mu_\tau(\theta)>\left(\frac{63}{64}-\rho\right)^2
 \left(\frac12-\rho\right)^2>\frac15,
\]
\[
 s_\pi(\theta)>\frac1{64}-\rho=\frac{15}{1024}>\frac1{100},
 \qquad
 s_K(\theta)>\frac12-\rho=\frac{511}{1024}>\frac25.
\]
For a time-two row put \(a=K_2(1\mid x)\).  Then \(|a-1/2|<\rho\), while the reward contrast exceeds \(1-2\rho\).  The binary variance identity gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{Y\sim K_2(\cdot\mid x)}\{r_2(x,Y)\}
 =a(1-a)\{r_2(x,1)-r_2(x,0)\}^2
 >\left(\frac14-\rho^2\right)(1-2\rho)^2>\frac15.
\]
The strict metric ball is relative-open, and every policy and transition cell at its center is strictly positive.  Finite inverse-transform action equations with independent coins realize all its policy kernels, while \(\texttt{lem:posterior-row-projection}\) realizes all transition posterior rows.  Thus the ball is an open family in the repaired compatible class and every displayed inequality is uniform on it.

For the objects in \(\texttt{def:quantitative-gap-neighborhood}\), the center \(\theta^\star\) obeys
\[
 [L_1(K,\tau),U_1(K,\tau)]=[-1/4,63/512],
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)=[-317/512,63/128],
\]
so \(\Delta_1^-(\theta^\star)=\Delta_1^+(\theta^\star)=189/512\).  Let \(\kappa=511/1024\).  Every \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\) satisfies
\[
 K_t(0\mid(0,0))>\kappa,
 \qquad
 \mu_\tau(\theta)>\left(\frac{63}{64}-\rho\right)^2
                         \left(\frac12-\rho\right)^2>\frac15,
\]
\[
 s_\pi(\theta)>\frac1{64}-\rho>\frac1{100},
 \qquad
 s_K(\theta)>\frac12-\rho>\frac25,
\]
\[
 V_{\mathrm{fd}}(\theta)>\left(\frac14-\rho^2\right)(1-2\rho)^2>\frac15,
 \qquad
 \Delta_1^-(\theta)>\frac14,
 \qquad
 \Delta_1^+(\theta)>\frac14.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\) is a relative-open, positive-mass family with uniformly interior policy and transition support, nonvanishing failure-driving conditional variance, and a uniform strict gap between the sharp shared-SCM interval and the internally defined coalitionwise relaxation.

defs.def:coalition-policy: For \(C\subseteq[H]\), set \(\alpha_t^C=\alpha_t^1\) when \(t\in C\) and \(\alpha_t^C=\alpha_t^0\) when \(t\notin C\).
defs.def:compatible-scm-class:
For fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\),
\[
 \mathfrak M(K)=\{\mathcal M:\mathcal M\text{ satisfies }
 \text{ass:fixed-initial-state},\ 
 \text{ass:markov-structural-equations},\ 
 \text{ass:independent-time-disturbances},\ 
 \text{ass:transition-marginals},\ 
 \text{ass:factual-policy-exogeneity},\ 
 \text{and }\text{ass:factual-action-positivity for every }t\in[H]\}.
\]
The notation \(\mathfrak M(K)\) abbreviates \(\mathfrak M(K;\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\).  The same fixed-ambient convention applies to the displayed transition-independent subclass and to every displayed \(\Theta_i\), \(L_i\), and \(U_i\) functional.  The policies are fixed external mechanisms and are never optimized model components.
defs.def:independent-coalition-outer-bound:
For \(i\in[H]\), define the internally constructed coalitionwise relaxation
\[
 \mathcal I_i^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)
 =\left[
 \sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}\omega_H(C)
 \left\{\inf_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_C(q)

Work on the fixed discrete stratum \(H=2\), \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), \(\tau=(0,0,0,0,0)\), and \(i=1\).  Write \(\theta=(K,r,\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}})\).  The interior center \(\theta^\star\) has \(K_t(y\mid s,a)=1/2\) for all cells, \(r_1((s,a),y)=0\), \(r_2((s,a),y)=y\), \(\pi_t(1\mid s)=1/64\) for every \(t,s\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(1\mid s)=1/4\), and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(1\mid s)=63/64\) for every \(s\).  All complementary action probabilities are determined by normalization.  Set \(\rho=1/1024\) and, with probability vectors ordered by \(0,1\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{\mathrm{pr}}(\theta,\theta^\star)=\max\Bigl\{
&\max_{t,x}\|K_t(\cdot\mid x)-(1/2,1/2)\|_1,
 \max_{x,y}|r_1(x,y)|,
 \max_{x,y}|r_2(x,y)-y|,\\
&\max_{t,s}\|\pi_t(\cdot\mid s)-(63/64,1/64)\|_1,\\
&\max_s\|\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(\cdot\mid s)-(3/4,1/4)\|_1,
 \max_s\|\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(\cdot\mid s)-(1/64,63/64)\|_1
\Bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Define \(\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\) to be the set of all valid kernel, reward, and policy primitives on this stratum satisfying \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}(\theta,\theta^\star)<\rho\).  Apart from the probability-simplex constraints, no continuous cell is held fixed.  For \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\), define
\[
 \mu_\tau(\theta)=\prod_{t=1}^2\pi_t(0\mid0)K_t(0\mid(0,0)),
\]
\[
 s_\pi(\theta)=\min_{t,s,a}\min\{\pi_t(a\mid s),\pi_{\mathrm{base},t}(a\mid s)\},
 \qquad
 s_K(\theta)=\min_{t,x,y}K_t(y\mid x),
\]
\[
 V_{\mathrm{fd}}(\theta)=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}
 \operatorname{Var}_{Y\sim K_2(\cdot\mid x)}\{r_2(x,Y)\},
\]

\[
 \Delta_1^-(\theta)=L_1(K,\tau)-\inf\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau),

At \(\theta^\star\), every factual transition probability is \(1/2\).  A binary nonfactual posterior success probability \(a\) is constrained only by \(a\in[0,1]\), so the fiber coordinates \(u,w,z,v\) range independently over \([0,1]\), while the factual rows are \(\delta_0\).

Put \(\eta=1/64\), \(\beta=63/64\), and \(\epsilon=1/4\).  The fixed initial state, external action coins, and deterministic terminal reward give the direct recursions
\[
 g_\varnothing=0,
 \qquad g_{\{1\}}=\epsilon u\{(1-\eta)z+\eta v\},
 \qquad g_{\{2\}}=\beta w,
\]
and
\[
 g_{\{1,2\}}=(1-\epsilon u)\beta w
 +\epsilon u\{(1-\beta)z+\beta v\}. \tag{1}
\]
For \(H=2\), both Shapley weights are \(1/2\), and \(\beta+\eta=1\).  Therefore
\[
 \Phi_1(q)=\frac{\epsilon u}{2}
 \left[\beta w-\{2-\beta-\eta\}z-(\beta+\eta)v\right]
 =\frac{u}{8}\left(\frac{63}{64}w-z-v\right). \tag{2}
\]
Its minimum is \(-1/4\), attained at \((u,w,z,v)=(1,0,1,1)\), and its maximum is \(63/512\), attained at \((1,1,0,0)\).  By the shared-endpoint definition and the repaired projection theorem, these are compatible-SCM endpoints with independent policy coins.

The separate coalition extrema from (1) are
\[
 \inf g_\varnothing=\sup g_\varnothing=0,
 \quad \inf g_{\{1\}}=0,
 \quad \sup g_{\{1\}}=\frac14,
 \quad \inf g_{\{2\}}=0,
 \quad \sup g_{\{2\}}=\frac{63}{64}.
\]
Also \(\inf g_{\{1,2\}}=0\), and setting all four row coordinates equal to one gives
\[
 \sup g_{\{1,2\}}=\beta+\epsilon(1-\beta)=\frac{253}{256}.
\]
The formula in \(\texttt{def:independent-coalition-outer-bound}\) consequently yields
\[
 \inf\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}=-\frac12\left(\frac14+\frac{253}{256}\right)
 =-\frac{317}{512},
 \qquad
 \sup\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}=\frac12\frac{63}{64}=\frac{63}{128}.
\]
Both excess widths are \(189/512\).

Now fix \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\), where \(\rho=1/1024\) and \(\kappa=511/1024\).  The metric definition gives
\[
 \delta(K,K^\star)<\rho,
 \qquad K_t(0\mid(0,0))>\frac12-\rho=\kappa. \tag{3}
\]
With center rewards and policies held fixed, complete returns lie in \([0,1]\).  The local modulus with \(H=2\) moves either shared endpoint by at most \(8\rho/\kappa\) when \(K^\star\) is replaced by \(K\).

Next hold \(K\), and hence its posterior fiber, fixed while changing rewards and policies.  For any coalition, maximally couple each external action draw.  The rowwise policy \(\ell^1\) discrepancies are below \(\rho\), so each action mismatch probability is below \(\rho/2\); a union bound over two actions gives path-law total variation below \(\rho\).  For fixed paths the two rewards differ by less than \(2\rho\).  Comparing first rewards on a common path and then center rewards across the coupled paths gives, uniformly in feasible \(q\),
\[
 |g_C(q;\theta)-g_C(q;K,r^\star,\pi^\star,\pi_{\mathrm{base}}^\star)|<3\rho. \tag{4}
\]
Because Shapley weights sum to one and every contribution is a difference of two returns, (4) moves \(\Phi_1\), and hence either shared extremum over the unchanged fiber, by less than \(6\rho\).  Thus each shared endpoint moves from its center value by at most
\[
 A=\frac{8\rho}{\kappa}+6\rho. \tag{5}
\]

The same \(A\) bounds either endpoint of the internal relaxation.  Indeed, the row-matching construction in the proof of \(\texttt{thm:local-positivity-modulus}\), applied between \(K^\star\) and \(K\), moves each posterior row by total variation below \(2\rho/\kappa\).  Sequential coupling over two transitions moves an extremum of any center-reward coalition return by at most \(4\rho/\kappa\); equation (4) adds \(3\rho\).  An endpoint of the internal interval has total absolute coefficient two, giving the bound \(2(4\rho/\kappa+3\rho)=A\).  Consequently
\[
 \min\{\Delta_1^-(\theta),\Delta_1^+(\theta)\}
 \ge\frac{189}{512}-2A
 =\frac{183}{512}-\frac{16}{511}>\frac14, \tag{6}
\]
where the last inequality is equivalent to \(55\cdot511>16\cdot512\).

The remaining certificates follow directly from the metric ball.  Coordinate differences are bounded by rowwise \(\ell^1\) differences, so
\[
 \mu_\tau(\theta)>\left(\frac{63}{64}-\rho\right)^2
 \left(\frac12-\rho\right)^2>\frac15,
\]
\[
 s_\pi(\theta)>\frac1{64}-\rho=\frac{15}{1024}>\frac1{100},
 \qquad
 s_K(\theta)>\frac12-\rho=\frac{511}{1024}>\frac25.
\]
For a time-two row put \(a=K_2(1\mid x)\).  Then \(|a-1/2|<\rho\), while the reward contrast exceeds \(1-2\rho\).  The binary variance identity gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{Y\sim K_2(\cdot\mid x)}\{r_2(x,Y)\}
 =a(1-a)\{r_2(x,1)-r_2(x,0)\}^2
 >\left(\frac14-\rho^2\right)(1-2\rho)^2>\frac15.
\]
The strict metric ball is relative-open, and every policy and transition cell at its center is strictly positive.  Finite inverse-transform action equations with independent coins realize all its policy kernels, while \(\texttt{lem:posterior-row-projection}\) realizes all transition posterior rows.  Thus the ball is an open family in the repaired compatible class and every displayed inequality is uniform on it.

thm:sparse-stochastic-trajectory-width.proof_tex:
Fix a stage \(t\notin J\).  By definition, \(p_t=1\).  For any nonfactual row \(x\ne x_t\), \(\texttt{def:posterior-row-fiber}\) gives
\[
 q_{t,x}(y)\le K_t(y\mid x)\quad\text{for every }y\in\mathcal S,
 \qquad
 \sum_yq_{t,x}(y)=\sum_yK_t(y\mid x)=1.
 \tag{1}
\]
Every difference \(K_t(y\mid x)-q_{t,x}(y)\) is nonnegative and their sum is zero, so every difference is zero.  Thus every nonfactual row at \(t\notin J\) is the singleton \(\{K_t(\cdot\mid x)\}\); the factual row is always the singleton \(\{\delta_{y_t}\}\).  At a stage in \(J\), at most the \(|\mathcal X|-1\) nonfactual rows can remain non-singleton.  The definition of \(m\) therefore yields
\[
 m\le\sum_{t\in J}(|\mathcal X|-1)=|J|(|\mathcal X|-1).
 \tag{2}
\]

Substitute every singleton selector by its unique row.  Write \(\mathcal D_t\) for the remaining decisions belonging to stage \(t\), so \(\sum_t|\mathcal D_t|=m\).  Use the explicit circuit constructed in \(\texttt{thm:optimization-preserving-compiler}\).  Its time-\(t\) policy, transition, and reward factors have scope contained in
\[
 \{W,S_t,A_t,S_{t+1}\}\cup\mathcal D_t.
 \tag{3}
\]
Eliminate in the backward order
\[
 A_H,S_{H+1},A_{H-1},S_H,\ldots,A_1,S_2,
 \tag{4}
\]
with a fixed initial state removed by its point-mass factor.  A direct backward induction shows that, before processing stage \(t\), the accumulated future message has scope contained in \(\{W,S_{t+1}\}\cup\bigcup_{u>t}\mathcal D_u\).  Combining it with (3) and eliminating the next variable in (4) leaves the same form with boundary state \(S_t\).  Consequently every path bucket contains \(W\), at most all \(m\) active decisions, and at most four nonglobal path variables.  Since the definition of constrained width excludes the global variable and subtracts one from the number of nonglobal live variables,
\[
 w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)\le (m+4)-1=m+3
 \tag{5}
\]
for all path buckets.  After (4), the \(W\)-bucket contains no path variable and at most the \(m\) decisions.  After summing \(W\), successive decision buckets also contain at most those \(m\) variables, so (5) bounds every bucket.

All chance variables in (4), followed by \(W\), are summed before any row selector is maximized.  Hence every chance variable sharing a current factor with a decision has already been summed, which is exactly legality of \(\preceq\).  Applying \(\texttt{thm:optimization-preserving-compiler}\) and (5) gives
\[
 O\!\left(H^2N d^{w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)+1}\right)
 \subseteq O\!\left(H^2N d^{m+4}\right).
 \tag{6}
\]
Singleton substitution does not change the objective: it merely inserts the unique feasible value.  The target theorem's backpointers therefore recover the joint assignment of the remaining selectors; restoring the unique singleton rows and applying its gluing sampler yields one compatible endpoint SCM shared across all worlds.

Finally, suppose \(|J|\le c\log H\) for a constant \(c\), while \(|\mathcal S|\), \(|\mathcal A|\), and \(d\) are fixed.  Then \(|\mathcal X|\) is fixed and (2) gives
\[
 d^{m+4}\le d^4H^{c(|\mathcal X|-1)\log d}.
\]
The explicit circuit has \(N=O(H|\mathcal X|)\) variables and factors for fixed alphabets, while the \(2H^2\)-state global selector is already accounted for by the leading \(H^2\) in (6).  Thus (6) is polynomial in \(H\), proving the stated sparse-stochastic tractability claim.

prop:active-chain-width-lower-bound.proof_tex:
Consider first the stated chain minor with summed chance variables \(Y_0,\ldots,Y_k\) and distinct active decisions \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_k\), where the stage-\(j\) factor has structural scope \(\{Y_{j-1},Y_j,Z_j\}\).  Additional factors or variables can only add scopes, so it suffices to work in the minor.

Let \(Z_r\) be the first of these decisions maximized by a legal order.  Before that maximization, both adjacent chance variables in every current factor containing \(Z_r\) must have been summed.  Summing \(Y_r\) combines the factors on the two incident chain edges and creates a factor whose scope contains \(Z_r\), \(Z_{r+1}\), and \(Y_{r+1}\) when \(r<k\).  Legality now forces \(Y_{r+1}\) to be summed before \(Z_r\); repeating the argument propagates to the right endpoint.  The identical argument through \(Y_{r-1}\) propagates to the left endpoint.  Thus all chain chance variables are summed before the first decision is maximized.  Successive chance elimination takes unions of the incident scopes, so, because the displayed dependences are genuine and the definition of the minor excludes numerical scope deletion, the resulting factor contains every \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_k\).  Equivalently, these decisions form an induced clique.  The bucket of the first decision therefore contains at least \(k\) nonglobal live variables, and the definition of width gives
\[
 w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)\ge k-1.
 \tag{1}
\]
For \(k=|J|\), this is the first assertion.

To show that the obstruction is realized inside the model rather than only by an abstract graph, fix any \(H\) and take \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), the all-zero factual state-action trajectory, and
\[
 K_t(y\mid x)=\frac12
 \qquad(t\in[H],\ x\in\mathcal X,\ y\in\mathcal S).
 \tag{2}
\]
Choose factual and baseline policies with both actions having positive probability at every state and time.  Then \(p_t=1/2<1\), so \(J=[H]\).  For every nonfactual row, the posterior constraints are
\[
 \frac12q_{t,x}(y)\le\frac12,
 \qquad q_{t,x}(0)+q_{t,x}(1)=1,
\]
and hence the row polytope is the full binary simplex with distinct vertices \(\delta_0\) and \(\delta_1\).  In particular the fiber is nonempty, and the converse direction of \(\texttt{lem:posterior-row-projection}\) supplies compatible response-table laws, independently sampled over time, so the example belongs to the stated Markov SCM class.  Select the row \(x=(0,1)\) at each stage.  In the factor circuit proved in \(\texttt{thm:optimization-preserving-compiler}\), after restricting the positive-probability action branch to \(A_t=1\), its transition factor genuinely depends on \(S_t\), \(S_{t+1}\), and that stage's row selector.  These factors form a fully active state-chain minor of length \(H\).  Equation (1) yields \(w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)\ge H-1\) for every legal order.  This obstruction persists under sufficiently small perturbations: strict positivity of both entries of each binary transition row and the inequality \(p_t<1\) imply that the two caps have sum \(1/p_t>1\), so their intersection with the binary simplex has positive length; strict action positivity and genuine factor dependence also persist.  The primitives in (2) and the policies are strictly interior, and hence they have a relative-open neighborhood of fully active chain instances.  Thus no bounded- or logarithmic-width guarantee holds uniformly over fully stochastic growing horizons.  This does not contradict the sparse result, whose premise requires only \(O(\log H)\) stages with \(p_t<1\).

Call a simplified endpoint circuit \(\mathfrak F_i^\sigma\) a fully active chain minor of length \(k\) if a factor-graph minor contains \(k\) distinct non-singleton row selectors, one at each of \(k\) active stages, linked successively by summed Markov chance variables, with every transition factor genuinely depending on its selector and the two adjacent chain variables.  If \(k=|J|\), then every legal sum-before-max order induces a clique on these selectors before the first of them is maximized and hence satisfies
\[
 w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)\ge |J|-1.
\]
Such fully active minors occur for every horizon in binary finite Markov SCMs with strictly interior transition and policy probabilities.  Therefore the ordinary fully stochastic growing-horizon class admits \(w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)=\Omega(|J|)=\Omega(H)\), so neither bounded nor logarithmic constrained width holds uniformly on that class.
node.justification: This proposition certifies that fully stochastic chains can force linear constrained width, preventing a false uniform polynomial-time claim.
node.gap: Published marginal-MAP hardness motivates caution, but the chain-minor obstruction and its realization inside this repaired SCM class are proved directly here.

lem:posterior-row-projection.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(K)\), with the fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\) understood as in \(\texttt{def:compatible-scm-class}\).  For \(t\in[H]\), set
\[
 E_t=\{R_t(x_t)=y_t\},\qquad B_t=\{A_t=a_t\},
 \qquad E=\bigcap_{t=1}^H E_t,\qquad B=\bigcap_{t=1}^H B_t.
 \tag{1}
\]
For \(t\ge1\), write \(E_{<t}=\bigcap_{u<t}E_u\) and \(B_{<t}=\bigcap_{u<t}B_u\), with empty intersections equal to the sure event.  By \(\texttt{ass:fixed-initial-state}\), \(S_1=s_1\) almost surely.  Inductively, on \(B_{<t}\cap E_{<t}\) one has \(S_t=s_t\): if this holds at \(t\), then \(B_t\) gives \((S_t,A_t)=x_t\), and \(E_t\), together with \(S_{t+1}=R_t(S_t,A_t)\) from \(\texttt{ass:markov-structural-equations}\), gives \(S_{t+1}=R_t(x_t)=y_t=s_{t+1}\).  Consequently,
\[
 \{\tau\}=B\cap E. \tag{2}
\]
This induction uses the prefix action and preceding transition events together; the transition events alone do not fix the realized state path.

Because \(R_t\) is a function of \(U_t\), \(\texttt{ass:independent-time-disturbances}\) makes \(R_1,\ldots,R_H\) mutually independent.  Let \(\lambda_t\) denote the law of \(R_t\).  Fix a response-table tuple \((r_1,\ldots,r_H)\in E\) having positive probability.  On \(B_{<t}\cap E_{<t}\), the preceding induction gives \(S_t=s_t\).  The full product-extension condition in \(\texttt{ass:factual-policy-exogeneity}\) makes \(V_t\) independent of the complete table tuple, all the events \(E_u\), and \(V_1,\ldots,V_{t-1}\).  Hence the structural lookup and its coordinate marginal give
\[
 \Pr\!\left(B_t\mid R_1=r_1,\ldots,R_H=r_H,E,B_{<t}\right)
 =\Pr\{G_t(s_t,V_t)=a_t\}=\pi_t(a_t\mid s_t). \tag{3}
\]
The chain rule applied sequentially to (3) yields
\[
 \Pr\!\left(B\mid R_1=r_1,\ldots,R_H=r_H,E\right)
 =c_\tau,
 \qquad c_\tau:=\prod_{t=1}^H\pi_t(a_t\mid s_t). \tag{4}
\]
Every factor in \(c_\tau\) is positive by \(\texttt{ass:factual-action-positivity}\).  Thus (4) is a positive likelihood constant that does not depend on the response-table tuple.  For every set \(D\) of table tuples, equations (2)--(4) give
\[
 \Pr\{(R_1,\ldots,R_H)\in D,\tau\}
 =c_\tau\Pr\{(R_1,\ldots,R_H)\in D,E\}. \tag{5}
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:transition-marginals}\) and \(\texttt{ass:factual-positivity}\),
\[
 \Pr(E_t)=K_t(y_t\mid x_t)=p_t>0. \tag{6}
\]
Independence of the response tables gives \(\Pr(E)=\prod_t p_t\).  Dividing (5) by \(\Pr(\tau)=c_\tau\prod_t p_t>0\) proves
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Law}(R_1,\ldots,R_H\mid\tau)
 &=\operatorname{Law}(R_1,\ldots,R_H\mid E)\\
 &=\bigotimes_{t=1}^H\operatorname{Law}(R_t\mid E_t).
 \end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]

Let \(\mathscr V_{\mathrm{coal}}=(V_t^C:t\in[H],C\subseteq[H])\).  This entire finite family is jointly independent of \((S_1,R_1,\ldots,R_H,V_1,\ldots,V_H)\) by \(\texttt{ass:factual-policy-exogeneity}\), while \(\{\tau\}\) is measurable with respect to the latter variables.  Therefore, for events \(A\) of coalition coins and \(D\) of response tables,
\[
 \Pr\{\mathscr V_{\mathrm{coal}}\in A,(R_1,\ldots,R_H)\in D\mid\tau\}
 =\Pr\{\mathscr V_{\mathrm{coal}}\in A\}\Pr\{(R_1,\ldots,R_H)\in D\mid\tau\}. \tag{8}
\]
Thus factual conditioning neither changes the coalition policy laws nor destroys their mutual independence or their independence from the posterior transition tables.

Define
\[
 q_{t,x}(y)=\Pr\{R_t(x)=y\mid E_t\}.
\]
Then \(q_{t,x_t}=\delta_{y_t}\).  For \(x\ne x_t\), the multiplication rule, event inclusion, and \(\texttt{ass:transition-marginals}\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 p_tq_{t,x}(y)
 &=\Pr\{R_t(x_t)=y_t,R_t(x)=y\}\\
 &\le \Pr\{R_t(x)=y\}=K_t(y\mid x).
 \end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
Conditioning is valid by (6), so every \(q_{t,x}\) is a probability mass function.  Equation (9) and the factual point mass are precisely the constraints in \(\texttt{def:posterior-row-fiber}\); hence \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\).  Equations (7)--(8) show that every coalition world uses its fixed kernel \(\alpha^C\), independent of the tables, and queries the same posterior transition kernel \(q\).

Conversely, fix \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\).  At time \(t\), draw \(Z_t\) with law \(K_t(\cdot\mid x_t)\) and set \(R_t(x_t)=Z_t\).  If \(p_t<1\), define, for \(x\ne x_t\),
\[
 h_{t,x}(y)=\frac{K_t(y\mid x)-p_tq_{t,x}(y)}{1-p_t}. \tag{10}
\]
The numerator is nonnegative by the fiber inequality, and
\[
 \sum_{y\in\mathcal S}h_{t,x}(y)=\frac{1-p_t}{1-p_t}=1, \tag{11}
\]
so \(h_{t,x}\in\Delta(\mathcal S)\).  Conditional on \(Z_t=y_t\), draw the nonfactual coordinates with respective laws \(q_{t,x}\); conditional on \(Z_t\ne y_t\), draw them with respective laws \(h_{t,x}\).  These conditional draws may be made independent across nonfactual rows.  This is one joint table law \(\lambda_t\), not a coalition-indexed law, and
\[
 \Pr\{R_t(x)=y\}=p_tq_{t,x}(y)+(1-p_t)h_{t,x}(y)=K_t(y\mid x). \tag{12}
\]
The factual coordinate has marginal \(K_t(\cdot\mid x_t)\) by construction.  If \(p_t=1\), the fiber inequalities \(q_{t,x}(y)\le K_t(y\mid x)\) and equality of the two total masses force \(q_{t,x}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\); use that row in the sole branch and omit (10).

Draw the constructed response tables independently over \(t\), put \(U_t=R_t\), and set \(F_t(x,U_t)=U_t(x)\).  This establishes the structural equations, timewise disturbance independence, and transition marginals.  Set \(S_1=s_1\).  It remains to append the policy mechanisms.  For each \(t\), draw \(V_t\in\mathcal A^{\mathcal S}\) with coordinate marginals \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid s)\), for example by taking its state coordinates independently; for each of the finitely many pairs \((t,C)\), draw \(V_t^C\in\mathcal A^{\mathcal S}\) with coordinate marginals \(\alpha_t^C(\cdot\mid s)\), again using a product over state coordinates.  Take the product of all these finite laws and the transition-table law, and define \(G_t(s,v)=v(s)\).  This realizes exactly the joint independence and all action-kernel marginals in \(\texttt{ass:factual-policy-exogeneity}\).  Because it is an external product extension, it exists for every transition-table law and therefore does not shrink the admissible transition-response class.  Although the product construction proves simultaneous existence for all \(2^H\) coalitions, a sampler stores only \(\pi\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base}}\), and the rule defining \(\alpha^C\), and generates the queried coin coordinates lazily; it need not store \(2^H\) mechanisms.

The resulting model satisfies every member property in \(\texttt{def:compatible-scm-class}\), and its factual trajectory has probability \(c_\tau\prod_t p_t>0\).  Applying (7) gives precisely the prescribed posterior rows.  The one law \(\lambda_t\) is shared by all nonfactual rows and every coalition world, completing the converse.

thm:sharp-shared-interval.proof_tex:
The array with factual rows \(q_{t,x_t}=\delta_{y_t}\) and nonfactual rows \(q_{t,x}=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\) is feasible, because \(0<p_t\le1\) and
\[
 p_tq_{t,x}(y)=p_tK_t(y\mid x)\le K_t(y\mid x).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\ne\varnothing\).  Every nonfactual factor is a simplex intersected with finitely many closed half-spaces, and every factual factor is a singleton.  Finiteness of \(\mathcal S\), \(\mathcal X\), and \([H]\) therefore makes \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) a compact convex polytope.

For a fixed coalition \(C\), expansion over the finite state-action paths gives
\[
 g_C(q)=\sum_{s_2,\ldots,s_{H+1}}\sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_H}
 \left\{\prod_{t=1}^H\alpha_t^C(a_t\mid s_t)
 q_{t,(s_t,a_t)}(s_{t+1})\right\}
 \left\{\sum_{t=1}^Hr_t((s_t,a_t),s_{t+1})\right\}. \tag{1}
\]
The external coalition coins in \(\texttt{ass:factual-policy-exogeneity}\) justify the policy factors in (1), and the deterministic rewards justify the last factor.  Formula (1) is a finite polynomial in \(q\), and a path uses at most one row at any fixed time; hence it is affine in each row separately.  By \(\texttt{def:shapley-coordinate}\), \(\Phi_i\) is also continuous and separately affine.

The two directions of \(\texttt{lem:posterior-row-projection}\), whose likelihood cancellation uses the fixed initial state and external policy coins, give
\[
 \Theta_i(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(q):q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\}. \tag{2}
\]
Compactness and continuity give a minimizer \(q^-\) and maximizer \(q^+\), whose values are \(L_i(K,\tau)\) and \(U_i(K,\tau)\) by \(\texttt{def:shared-endpoints}\).  For \(s\in[0,1]\), convexity gives \(q(s)=(1-s)q^-+sq^+\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\), and \(s\mapsto\Phi_i(q(s))\) is continuous.  The intermediate-value property therefore fills every value between the endpoint values.  Conversely no value in (2) can lie outside the defining extrema.  Hence
\[
 \Theta_i(K,\tau)=[L_i(K,\tau),U_i(K,\tau)]. \tag{3}
\]
Applying the converse gluing in \(\texttt{lem:posterior-row-projection}\) to \(q^-\), \(q^+\), and any interpolating \(q(s)\) gives models in the repaired \(\mathfrak M(K)\); their fixed initial state and factual and coalition action coins are supplied exactly as in that lemma.  Thus (3) is a causal identified-set equality and both endpoints are attained by one compatible transition SCM shared across coalition worlds.

For the row-vertex assertion, start with either endpoint optimizer and one row factor \(P\).  With all other rows fixed, separate affineness gives an affine objective \(f\) on \(P\).  If an optimizing row lies in the relative interior of a nontrivial segment \([v_0,v_1]\subseteq P\), then its value is a strict convex combination of \(f(v_0)\) and \(f(v_1)\).  Optimality forces both endpoint values to equal the optimum.  Replace the row by an endpoint lying in a proper face and repeat.  The face dimension strictly decreases, so after finitely many replacements the row is a vertex without changing the global objective.  Repeating over the finitely many rows produces an optimizer all of whose rows are vertices; factual singleton rows already are vertices.

Finally, the gluing proof is a compact sampler.  It stores \(K_t(\cdot\mid x_t)\), the selected \(q_{t,x}\), and, when \(p_t<1\), the residual rows in equation (7) of that proof.  It samples the factual coordinate first and the remaining coordinates conditionally from the posterior or residual rows.  The storage is \(O(H|\mathcal X||\mathcal S|)\) probabilities, and it does not list the generally exponential mass table on \(\mathcal S^{\mathcal X}\).  Adding the independent finite action-coin samplers requires only the displayed policy tables and does not change this response-table storage bound.

prop:exact-coalition-compression.proof_tex:
Fix \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\), and let \(m=H-1\).  Under the definition of \(G_i^b(z,q)\), each \(t\ne i\) independently selects \(\alpha_t^1\) with probability \(z\) and \(\alpha_t^0\) with probability \(1-z\), while membership of \(i\) is fixed at \(b\).  Expanding these independent selections and using \(\text{def:coalition-policy}\) gives
\[
 G_i^0(z,q)=\sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}
 z^{|C|}(1-z)^{m-|C|}g_C(q),
\]
\[
 G_i^1(z,q)=\sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}
 z^{|C|}(1-z)^{m-|C|}g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q).
\]
Their difference \(P_i(z,q)\) is therefore a polynomial of degree at most \(m=H-1\).  Repeated integration by parts, with the boundary cases at zero and one, gives for \(0\le k\le m\)
\[
 \int_0^1 z^k(1-z)^{m-k}\,dz
 =\frac{k!(m-k)!}{(m+1)!}.
\]
Integrating the finite expansion term by term and invoking \(\text{def:shapley-coordinate}\) yields
\[
 \int_0^1P_i(z,q)\,dz
 =\sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}
 \omega_H(C)\{g_C(q)-g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q)\}
 =\Phi_i(q).
\]

The \(H\) pairwise distinct nodes \(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_H\) interpolate every polynomial of degree at most \(H-1\): explicitly,
\[
 P_i(z,q)=\sum_{j=1}^H P_i(\zeta_j,q)\ell_j(z).
\]
After integration, the definition \(\nu_j=\int_0^1\ell_j(z)\,dz\) gives
\[
 \Phi_i(q)=\sum_{j=1}^H\nu_jP_i(\zeta_j,q)=\mathsf Q_i(q),
\]
which is \(\text{def:quadrature-representation}\).  This includes \(H=1\), when both sides are the constant marginal contribution.

For one fixed \(z\) and branch \(b\), forward recursion keeps the current state distribution and, at every time, sums over \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), and \(y\in\mathcal S\).  It therefore uses \(O(H|\mathcal S|^2|\mathcal A|)\) arithmetic operations and sums rewards during the same recursion.  There are two branches at each of \(H\) nodes, so all values in the last display cost \(O(H^2|\mathcal S|^2|\mathcal A|)\) operations.  No coalition or state-path list is formed.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\), \(P_i(z,q)\) has degree at most \(H-1\) in \(z\), and \(\Phi_i(q)=\int_0^1P_i(z,q)\,dz=\sum_{j=1}^H\nu_jP_i(\zeta_j,q)\). For fixed \(q\), all terms are evaluated exactly in \(O(H^2|\mathcal S|^2|\mathcal A|)\) arithmetic operations, without enumerating coalitions or state paths.

prop:affine-nonnegative-lift.proof_tex:
For each \(t\), \(M_t-m_t\ge0\).  If \(R=\sum_t(M_t-m_t)=0\), every summand vanishes, so \(r_t(x,y)=m_t=M_t\) for all \(x,y\).  Every coalition return is then the same constant \(\sum_tm_t\).  The signed differences in \(\text{def:shapley-coordinate}\) vanish, and \(L_i=U_i=0\) by \(\text{def:shared-endpoints}\).

Assume henceforth that \(R>0\).  On any complete path with total reward \(G'=\sum_tr_t((s'_t,a'_t),s'_{t+1})\), the definitions give
\[
 \sum_{t=1}^Hh_t^+=\frac{G'-\sum_tm_t}{R},\qquad
 \sum_{t=1}^Hh_t^-=\frac{\sum_tM_t-G'}{R}.
\]
The stagewise bounds \(m_t\le r_t\le M_t\) imply that the first quantity lies in \([0,1]\), and since \(R=\sum_tM_t-\sum_tm_t\), the second equals one minus the first.  Taking the Markov expectation in branch \((j,b)\) proves
\[
 0\le h_{jb}(q)\le1,
 \qquad
 h_{jb}(q)=\frac{G_i^b(\zeta_j,q)-\sum_tm_t}{R}.
\]

For a real number \(a\), the summand used in \(F_i^\sigma\) is \(ah\) if \(a\ge0\), and \(|a|(1-h)=|a|+ah\) if \(a<0\).  For each \(j\), the two coefficients \(a_{j0}^\sigma=\sigma\nu_j\) and \(a_{j1}^\sigma=-\sigma\nu_j\) have total negative-part magnitude \(|\nu_j|\).  Therefore \(\text{def:nonnegative-endpoint-objectives}\) implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F_i^\sigma(q)
 &=C_\nu+\sum_{j=1}^H\sum_{b=0}^1a_{jb}^\sigma h_{jb}(q)\\
 &=C_\nu+\frac{\sigma}{R}\sum_{j=1}^H\nu_j
       \{G_i^0(\zeta_j,q)-G_i^1(\zeta_j,q)\}\\
 &=C_\nu+\frac{\sigma}{R}\Phi_i(q),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality is \(\text{prop:exact-coalition-compression}\).  All terms in the defining expression of \(F_i^\sigma\) are nonnegative because \(0\le h_{jb}\le1\).  Maximizing the identity over the same set \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) gives
\[
 V_{+1}=C_\nu+\frac{U_i}{R},\qquad
 V_{-1}=C_\nu-\frac{L_i}{R},
\]
and rearrangement proves the two endpoint formulas.

thm:open-family-shared-gap.proof_tex:
In \(\mathfrak G_\varepsilon\), \(p_1=p_2=1/2\).  For a binary nonfactual row with marginal \((1/2,1/2)\), \(\texttt{def:posterior-row-fiber}\) imposes only
\[
 \tfrac12q(0)\le\tfrac12,\qquad \tfrac12q(1)\le\tfrac12,
 \qquad q(0)+q(1)=1,
\]
so its success coordinate ranges over \([0,1]\).  Product structure makes \(u,w,z,v\) independent coordinates of \([0,1]^4\), while both factual rows are \(\delta_0\).

The first reward is zero and the second is the terminal next state.  Under the externally randomized policies in the repaired model class, direct recursion gives
\[
 g_\varnothing=0,
 \qquad g_{\{1\}}=\varepsilon uz,
 \qquad g_{\{2\}}=w,
 \qquad g_{\{1,2\}}=(1-\varepsilon u)w+\varepsilon uv. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, the time-one baseline chooses action one with probability \(\varepsilon\); conditional on that action it reaches state one with probability \(u\).  The retained time-two action is zero, with success probability \(z\), whereas a time-two switch uses action one, with success probability \(w\) from state zero and \(v\) from state one.  For \(H=2\), both Shapley weights equal \(1/2\), so (1) and \(\texttt{def:shapley-coordinate}\) yield
\[
 \Phi_1(q)=\frac12\{g_\varnothing-g_{\{1\}}+g_{\{2\}}-g_{\{1,2\}}\}
 =\frac{\varepsilon u}{2}(w-z-v). \tag{2}
\]
The maximum of (2) is \(\varepsilon/2\), attained at \((u,w,z,v)=(1,1,0,0)\), and its minimum is \(-\varepsilon\), attained at \((1,0,1,1)\).  By \(\texttt{thm:sharp-shared-interval}\), the gluing sampler, completed by the external policy coins, gives compatible shared-SCM witnesses for both assignments.

The internal relaxation gives each distinct coalition return its own posterior-kernel copy.  Equations (1) imply
\[
 g_\varnothing\in\{0\},\qquad g_{\{1\}}\in[0,\varepsilon],
 \qquad g_{\{2\}}\in[0,1],\qquad g_{\{1,2\}}\in[0,1],
\]
and every displayed endpoint is attainable in its respective copy.  Substitution into \(\texttt{def:independent-coalition-outer-bound}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)
 =\left[-\frac{1+\varepsilon}{2},\frac12\right].
\]
Both excess widths relative to \([-\varepsilon,\varepsilon/2]\) equal \((1-\varepsilon)/2>0\).

At \(\varepsilon=1/4\), the positive-gap set contains policy-interior points arbitrarily close to the displayed boundary tuple.  Keep \(K,r\), and the time-one baseline fixed, and, for \(0\le c\le1/64\), set \(\pi_t(1\mid s)=c\) and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(1\mid s)=1-c\) for every \(t,s\).  Repeating the recursion with \(\eta=c\) and \(\beta=1-c\) gives
\[
 [L_1,U_1]=\left[-\frac14,\frac{1-c}{8}\right],
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}
 =\left[-\frac58+\frac{3c}{8},\frac{1-c}{2}\right]. \tag{3}
\]
Both excess widths in (3) equal \(3(1-c)/8>0\), and every policy cell is positive when \(c>0\).

The two excess-width maps are continuous on a relative neighborhood with positive factual transition cells.  To see this directly, \(\texttt{thm:local-positivity-modulus}\) controls the shared endpoints under changes of \(K\).  With a posterior fiber fixed, every coalition return is a finite polynomial in rewards, policies, and posterior rows, hence uniformly continuous on the finite compact product.  The row-matching construction in the modulus proof gives Hausdorff continuity of the posterior fibers, and matching an optimizer in both directions transfers uniform continuity to every coalition-return infimum and supremum.  Finite sums and differences preserve continuity.  Since the two slacks at the boundary tuple equal \(3/8\), their positivity set contains a relative-open neighborhood of that tuple; equation (3) shows that this neighborhood may be chosen to meet the policy interior.

The explicit interior center \(\theta^\star\) in \(\texttt{def:quantitative-gap-neighborhood}\) is the point \(c=1/64\) on this segment.  The theorem \(\texttt{thm:quantitative-gap-neighborhood}\) further proves that every primitive tuple in the relative-open ball \(\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\) has positive factual mass and both excess widths greater than \(1/4\).  Finite inverse-transform action maps and independent coins realize every policy in that ball, and the transition gluing theorem realizes every posterior optimizer.  Thus the strict separation persists on the claimed open family inside the repaired SCM class, without varying policy-response or reward-noise coupling.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(0<\varepsilon<1\), in \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\) write \(u=q_{1,(0,1)}(1)\), \(w=q_{2,(0,1)}(1)\), \(z=q_{2,(1,0)}(1)\), and \(v=q_{2,(1,1)}(1)\). The posterior fiber makes \(u,w,z,v\) independently range over \([0,1]\), while \(q_{t,(0,0)}=\delta_0\). Direct recursion gives \(g_{\varnothing}=0\), \(g_{\{1\}}=\varepsilon uz\), \(g_{\{2\}}=w\), and \(g_{\{1,2\}}=(1-\varepsilon u)w+\varepsilon uv\), so \(\Phi_1=(\varepsilon u/2)(w-z-v)\). Thus \(U_1=\varepsilon/2\) is attained at \((u,w,z,v)=(1,1,0,0)\), and \(L_1=-\varepsilon\) is attained at \((1,0,1,1)\). With independent coalition copies, \(g_{\varnothing}\in\{0\}\), \(g_{\{1\}}\in[0,\varepsilon]\), \(g_{\{2\}}\in[0,1]\), and \(g_{\{1,2\}}\in[0,1]\), whence \(\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}=[-(1+\varepsilon)/2,1/2]\). Its lower and upper excess widths over the shared interval both equal \((1-\varepsilon)/2>0\). At \(\varepsilon=1/4\), continuity of extrema over compact continuously varying fibers yields a relative neighborhood of the full primitive tuple, restricted to positive factual cells and valid probability simplices and containing interior policy points, on which both slacks remain positive.

defs.def:compatible-scm-class:
For fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\),
\[
 \mathfrak M(K)=\{\mathcal M:\mathcal M\text{ satisfies }
 \text{ass:fixed-initial-state},\ 
 \text{ass:markov-structural-equations},\ 
 \text{ass:independent-time-disturbances},\ 
 \text{ass:transition-marginals},\ 
 \text{ass:factual-policy-exogeneity},\ 
 \text{and }\text{ass:factual-action-positivity for every }t\in[H]\}.
\]
The notation \(\mathfrak M(K)\) abbreviates \(\mathfrak M(K;\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\).  The same fixed-ambient convention applies to the displayed transition-independent subclass and to every displayed \(\Theta_i\), \(L_i\), and \(U_i\) functional.  The policies are fixed external mechanisms and are never optimized model components.
defs.def:independent-coalition-outer-bound:
For \(i\in[H]\), define the internally constructed coalitionwise relaxation
\[
 \mathcal I_i^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)
 =\left[
 \sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}\omega_H(C)
 \left\{\inf_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_C(q)
       -\sup_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q)\right\},
 \sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}\omega_H(C)
 \left\{\sup_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_C(q)
       -\inf_{q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)}g_{C\cup\{i\}}(q)\right\}
 \right].
\]
Thus every distinct coalition return is optimized over its own copy of the posterior fiber before the signed Shapley sum is formed.  This relaxation is defined internally for comparison; its definition does not attribute this operation to an external estimator or workflow.

defs.def:quantitative-gap-neighborhood:
Work on the fixed discrete stratum \(H=2\), \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), \(\tau=(0,0,0,0,0)\), and \(i=1\).  Write \(\theta=(K,r,\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}})\).  The interior center \(\theta^\star\) has \(K_t(y\mid s,a)=1/2\) for all cells, \(r_1((s,a),y)=0\), \(r_2((s,a),y)=y\), \(\pi_t(1\mid s)=1/64\) for every \(t,s\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(1\mid s)=1/4\), and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(1\mid s)=63/64\) for every \(s\).  All complementary action probabilities are determined by normalization.  Set \(\rho=1/1024\) and, with probability vectors ordered by \(0,1\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{\mathrm{pr}}(\theta,\theta^\star)=\max\Bigl\{
&\max_{t,x}\|K_t(\cdot\mid x)-(1/2,1/2)\|_1,
 \max_{x,y}|r_1(x,y)|,
 \max_{x,y}|r_2(x,y)-y|,\\
&\max_{t,s}\|\pi_t(\cdot\mid s)-(63/64,1/64)\|_1,\\
&\max_s\|\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(\cdot\mid s)-(3/4,1/4)\|_1,
 \max_s\|\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(\cdot\mid s)-(1/64,63/64)\|_1
\Bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Define \(\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\) to be the set of all valid kernel, reward, and policy primitives on this stratum satisfying \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}(\theta,\theta^\star)<\rho\).  Apart from the probability-simplex constraints, no continuous cell is held fixed.  For \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho(\theta^\star)\), define
\[
 \mu_\tau(\theta)=\prod_{t=1}^2\pi_t(0\mid0)K_t(0\mid(0,0)),
\]
\[
 s_\pi(\theta)=\min_{t,s,a}\min\{\pi_t(a\mid s),\pi_{\mathrm{base},t}(a\mid s)\},
 \qquad
 s_K(\theta)=\min_{t,x,y}K_t(y\mid x),
\]
\[
 V_{\mathrm{fd}}(\theta)=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}
 \operatorname{Var}_{Y\sim K_2(\cdot\mid x)}\{r_2(x,Y)\},
\]
and the lower and upper excess widths of the internal relaxation by
\[
 \Delta_1^-(\theta)=L_1(K,\tau)-\inf\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau),
 \qquad
 \Delta_1^+(\theta)=\sup\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{ind}}(K,\tau)-U_1(K,\tau).
\]
defs.def:strict-gap-family: For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\) is the primitive tuple \(H=2\), \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), \(S_1=0\), \(\tau=(0,0,0,0,0)\), \(K_t(y\mid s,a)=1/2\) for every \(t,s,a,y\), \(r_1((s,a),y)=0\), \(r_2((s,a),y)=y\), and \(i=1\). For every state and time, \(\pi_t(0\mid s)=1\). For both states, \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(1\mid s)=\varepsilon\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},1}(0\mid s)=1-\varepsilon\), and \(\pi_{\mathrm{base},2}(1\mid s)=1\).

assumptions.ass:factual-action-positivity: For every \(t\in[H]\), the factual-policy cell satisfies \(\pi_t(a_t\mid s_t)>0\).
assumptions.ass:factual-policy-exogeneity: On a finite product extension of the transition probability space, the complete family \(\{V_t:t\in[H]\}\cup\{V_t^C:t\in[H],\ C\subseteq[H]\}\) is mutually independent and jointly independent of \((S_1,U_1,\ldots,U_H)\), with each \(V_t\in\mathcal A^{\mathcal S}\) satisfying \(\Pr\{V_t(s)=a\}=\pi_t(a\mid s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\) and entering the factual equation \(A_t=G_t(S_t,V_t)=V_t(S_t)\), and with each \(V_t^C\in\mathcal A^{\mathcal S}\) satisfying \(\Pr\{V_t^C(s)=a\}=\alpha_t^C(a\mid s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\) and generating the state-contingent action sample \(A_t=V_t^C(S_t)\) in coalition world \(C\).
assumptions.ass:fixed-initial-state: The initial state is fixed: \(S_1=s_1\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:markov-structural-equations: The environment transition equation at time \(t\) is \(S_{t+1}=F_t(S_t,A_t,U_t)\).
assumptions.ass:transition-marginals: For every \(t\in[H]\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(y\in\mathcal S\), \(\Pr\{F_t(x,U_t)=y\}=K_t(y\mid x)\).

thm:simultaneous-confidence-fiber.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mathcal E=\{K\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)\}.
\]
The assumed simultaneous coverage gives \(\Pr_K(\mathcal E)\ge1-\alpha\) under \(\text{ass:fixed-row-multinomial-sampling}\).  On \(\mathcal E\), every prespecified trajectory having positive probability under \(K\) makes the true kernel admissible in the defining optimizations for \(L_i^\alpha\) and \(U_i^\alpha\).  Hence, directly from \(\text{def:confidence-fiber-endpoints}\),
\[
 L_i^\alpha\le L_i(K,\tau)\le U_i(K,\tau)\le U_i^\alpha.
\]
The event \(\mathcal E\) depends only on the transition kernel, not on \(i\), \(\tau\), or the specified policy pair.  The same event therefore proves all asserted containments simultaneously; no additional union bound over queries is needed.  By \(\text{thm:sharp-shared-interval}\), these are containments of the whole population identified sets, not merely of selected point values.

For the geometric assertion, write the rowwise product confidence region as \(\prod_{t,x}\mathcal C_{t,x}\), and set
\[
 p_t^- =\min_{k\in\mathcal C_{t,x_t}}k(y_t),
 \qquad
 p_t^+ =\max_{k\in\mathcal C_{t,x_t}}k(y_t).
\]
The proposed statement assumes that the row polytopes are nonempty and that \(p_t^+>0\) for every \(t\), precisely the conditions needed for a nonempty positive-evidence confidence fiber.  If \(p_t^->0\), define, for \(x\ne x_t\),
\[
 \mathcal Q_{t,x}
 =\{q_x\in\Delta(\mathcal S):
       \exists k_x\in\mathcal C_{t,x}\text{ such that }
       p_t^-q_x(y)\le k_x(y)\text{ for all }y\}.
\]
This is the projection of an explicitly given bounded polyhedron in \((q_x,k_x)\), hence is an explicit polytope.  If \(q_x\) is feasible for some common factual probability \(p_t\ge p_t^-\), it is feasible at \(p_t^-\) with the same \(k_x\).  Conversely, choose a factual confidence row attaining \(p_t^-\) and, independently for each alternate row, a witnessing \(k_x\).  Product structure of the confidence region then supplies a single kernel \(K'\), with the same \(p_t^-\) for every alternate row.  Thus the union of posterior fibers is exactly
\[
 \{q_{t,x_t}=\delta_{y_t}\}\times
 \prod_{x\ne x_t}\mathcal Q_{t,x}
\]
at time \(t\), and the product over times is exact as well.

Suppose instead that \(p_t^-=0<p_t^+\), and put
\[
 J_{t,x}=\{y\in\mathcal S:\exists k\in\mathcal C_{t,x}
                    \text{ with }k(y)>0\}.
\]
For every positive factual value \(p\), feasibility \(pq_x(y)\le k_x(y)\) forces \(q_x(y)=0\) when \(y\notin J_{t,x}\).  This proves that the closure is contained in the simplex supported on \(J_{t,x}\).  Conversely, by convexity of \(\mathcal C_{t,x}\), averaging one witness for each member of the finite set \(J_{t,x}\) gives a single \(k_x^*\in\mathcal C_{t,x}\) positive on all of \(J_{t,x}\).  For any \(q_x\) supported there, all inequalities \(pq_x(y)\le k_x^*(y)\) hold for sufficiently small \(p>0\).  There are finitely many alternate rows, so one sufficiently small \(p\) works for all of them.  The projection of the convex factual-row polytope onto its \(y_t\)-coordinate is the interval \([0,p_t^+]\), so that common positive \(p\) is attainable.  Letting \(p\downarrow0\) proves that the closure is the claimed product of support simplices.  The same reasoning independently at each time completes the product-fiber characterization.

If \(p_t^+=0\), the set of confidence kernels satisfying the positive-evidence restriction is empty at that time, and its closure is empty rather than a support simplex.  This explicit countercase is why the positive-maximum clause in the proposed statement is necessary.

snapshot.stmt: If \(\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)\) has simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\alpha\), then with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), \([L_i(K,\tau),U_i(K,\tau)]\subseteq[L_i^{\alpha},U_i^{\alpha}]\) simultaneously for every \(i\in[H]\) and every prespecified positive-probability factual trajectory and policy pair. On every realized confidence region whose rowwise polytopes are nonempty and for which each factual confidence row attains a positive value of \(K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)\), the confidence posterior-row fiber is a product of explicit local polytopes when every factual confidence-cell minimum is positive; when the minimum at time \(t\) is zero, the closure of that time block is the product, over its nonfactual rows, of simplices supported on next states having positive attainable marginal probability.

defs.def:confidence-fiber-endpoints: \(L_i^{\alpha}=\inf_{K'\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K):\,K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)>0\ \forall t}L_i(K',\tau)\) and \(U_i^{\alpha}=\sup_{K'\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K):\,K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)>0\ \forall t}U_i(K',\tau)\), with closure in posterior-row space when a confidence fiber approaches a zero factual cell.

assumptions.ass:fixed-row-multinomial-sampling: Conditional on each row \((t,x)\), the \(n_{t,x}\) observed next states are independent draws from \(K_t(\cdot\mid x)\).

thm:local-positivity-modulus.proof_tex:
Put \(\delta=\delta(K,K')\).  Fix \(t\), write \(p=K_t(y_t\mid x_t)\), \(p'=K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)\), and take a nonfactual row \(x\ne x_t\).  Let \(k=K_t(\cdot\mid x)\), \(k'=K'_t(\cdot\mid x)\), and let \(q\) be feasible for the \(K\)-fiber.  Define
\[
 a(y)=\min\{q(y),k'(y)/p'\},
 \qquad d_0=1-\sum_ya(y).
\]
Division is valid because \(p'\ge\kappa>0\).  Since \(pq(y)\le k(y)\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_0
 &=\frac1{p'}\sum_y\bigl(p'q(y)-k'(y)\bigr)_+\\
 &\le\frac{|p'-p|+\|k-k'\|_1}{p'}
 \le\frac{2\delta}{\kappa}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
For the middle inequality, decompose \(p'q-k'=(p'-p)q+(pq-k)+(k-k')\); the middle term is coordinatewise nonpositive, while the positive parts of the other two terms total at most \(|p'-p|\) and \(\|k-k'\|_1\).  Both are at most \(\delta\) by its definition.

The unused upper-cap capacity is
\[
 \sum_y\{k'(y)/p'-a(y)\}=1/p'-1+d_0\ge d_0.
\]
Distribute mass \(d_0\) within those capacities and call the added vector \(b\).  Then \(q'=a+b\) is in the \(K'\)-row factor and
\[
 \|q-q'\|_1\le\|q-a\|_1+\|b\|_1=2d_0
 \le\frac{4\delta}{\kappa},
 \qquad \operatorname{TV}(q,q')\le\frac{2\delta}{\kappa}. \tag{2}
\]
The factual posterior rows agree at \(\delta_{y_t}\).  Applying this construction to every nonfactual row and time maps any \(q\in\mathcal B(K,\tau)\) to a \(q'\in\mathcal B(K',\tau)\) with the uniform row bound (2).  Interchanging \(K,K'\) gives the reverse fiber approximation.

Fix a coalition policy and couple its paths under \(q,q'\).  Both start at \(s_1\) by \(\texttt{ass:fixed-initial-state}\).  While the states agree, use the same fresh external action coin, which is licensed by \(\texttt{ass:factual-policy-exogeneity}\), and maximally couple the two next-state rows.  Equation (2) bounds the conditional probability of a first next-state mismatch by \(2\delta/\kappa\) at every transition.  A union bound over \(H\) transitions therefore bounds the complete-path mismatch probability by \(2H\delta/\kappa\).  Equal paths have equal deterministic returns, while unequal complete returns differ by at most \(D\).  Hence, for every coalition,
\[
 |g_C(q)-g_C(q')|\le\frac{2DH\delta}{\kappa}. \tag{3}
\]
The weights are nonnegative, and their total is
\[
 \sum_{C\subseteq[H]\setminus\{i\}}\omega_H(C)
 =\sum_{k=0}^{H-1}{H-1\choose k}\frac{k!(H-k-1)!}{H!}=1. \tag{4}
\]
Thus \(\texttt{def:shapley-coordinate}\) and (3) give
\[
 |\Phi_i(q)-\Phi_i(q')|
 \le\frac{4DH\delta}{\kappa}. \tag{5}
\]

By \(\texttt{thm:sharp-shared-interval}\), both extrema are attained and represent the causal identified-set endpoints in the repaired class.  Map a maximizer over the \(K\)-fiber into the \(K'\)-fiber and apply (5); then reverse the kernels.  This proves the two-sided upper-endpoint bound.  Applying the same argument to minimizers proves
\[
 \max\left\{|L_i(K,\tau)-L_i(K',\tau)|,
 |U_i(K,\tau)-U_i(K',\tau)|\right\}
 \le\frac{4DH}{\kappa}\delta(K,K'). \tag{6}
\]

By definition, \(r_{\mathrm{pos}}(\kappa)=\kappa/2\).  If only the \(K\)-cells are initially at least \(\kappa\) and \(\delta(K,K')<\kappa/2\), then
\[
 K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge K_t(y_t\mid x_t)-\delta(K,K')>\kappa/2.
\]
Both kernels consequently satisfy the first part with common lower bound \(\kappa/2\), so for \(E_i\in\{L_i,U_i\}\),
\[
 |E_i(K',\tau)-E_i(K,\tau)|
 \le\frac{8DH}{\kappa}\delta(K,K'). \tag{7}
\]

On the coverage event, the true kernel belongs to the explicit confidence product.  If \(r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)<\kappa/2\), every kernel in that product is within the certified radius, has positive factual cells, and obeys (7).  Taking the infimum of its lower endpoints and the supremum of its upper endpoints, while using the true kernel as a feasible point, gives
\[
 L_i(K,\tau)-\frac{8DH}{\kappa}r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)
 \le L_i^\alpha\le L_i(K,\tau)
\]
and
\[
 U_i(K,\tau)\le U_i^\alpha
 \le U_i(K,\tau)+\frac{8DH}{\kappa}r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K).
\]
The empty-fiber fallback is irrelevant on this event because the confidence product contains the positive-evidence true kernel.

Finally, on \(\delta(\widehat K,K)<\kappa/2\), equation (7) with \(K'=\widehat K\) bounds each plug-in error by \(8DH\delta(\widehat K,K)/\kappa\).  Uniform convergence of this discrepancy in probability therefore implies uniform plug-in consistency.  The two confidence displays give uniform confidence-endpoint convergence on any coverage events for which \(r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)\) converges uniformly to zero.  No differentiability, normality, or adaptive-sampling assertion is used.

prop:counterfactual-independence-reducti.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)\).  The subclass inherits the fixed initial state, the complete joint external policy-coin family, factual-action positivity, and the transition assumptions from \(\mathfrak M(K)\).  Therefore \(\texttt{lem:posterior-row-projection}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(R_1,\ldots,R_H\mid\tau)
 =\bigotimes_{t=1}^H\operatorname{Law}(R_t\mid R_t(x_t)=y_t). \tag{1}
\]
At time \(t\), \(\texttt{ass:within-time-row-independence}\) states mutual independence of the whole finite family \((R_t(x))_{x\in\mathcal X}\).  Hence the vector of all nonfactual coordinates is jointly independent of \(R_t(x_t)\).  Since \(p_t>0\), conditioning on the factual coordinate and using \(\texttt{ass:transition-marginals}\) gives, for \(x\ne x_t\),
\[
 \Pr\{R_t(x)=y\mid R_t(x_t)=y_t\}
 =\Pr\{R_t(x)=y\}=K_t(y\mid x). \tag{2}
\]
On the conditioned coordinate itself the law is \(\delta_{y_t}\).  Moreover, mutual independence makes the conditional joint law of all nonfactual coordinates the product of their transition marginals.  Equations (1)--(2) therefore make the transition posterior kernel uniquely equal to \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\) in \(\texttt{def:counterfactual-independent-target}\).

This kernel is feasible in \(\mathcal B(K,\tau)\), since its factual row is the required point mass and, for \(x\ne x_t\),
\[
 p_tq_{t,x}^{\mathrm{CI}}(y)=p_tK_t(y\mid x)\le K_t(y\mid x).
\]
By the joint product-extension condition, the whole coalition-coin family remains mutually independent and independent of the transition tables after factual conditioning.  Thus every model in the subclass evaluates every coalition by its fixed kernel \(\alpha^C\) and the same Markov recursion with \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\).  Consequently
\[
 \Theta_i^{\mathrm{CI}}(K,\tau)=\{\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\}.
\]
Feasibility of \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\) and \(\texttt{thm:sharp-shared-interval}\) yield \(\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\in\Theta_i(K,\tau)\), proving the asserted inclusion.  This reduction selects only the transition-row coupling inside the explicitly externally randomized, deterministic-reward model; it does not claim to remove the full policy- or reward-counterfactual-independence scheme of the published model.

The subclass is nonempty.  At each time, draw the coordinates \(R_t(x)\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), mutually independently with respective laws \(K_t(\cdot\mid x)\); take the product over times and append the joint external factual and coalition policy-coin family exactly as in the converse of \(\texttt{lem:posterior-row-projection}\).  The resulting model satisfies every member property of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{CI}}(K)\).

Finally, at the transition component, the published full scheme of Li, Lee, and Bareinboim projects to the same selected posterior \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\): its mutual independence of transition-response coordinates gives exactly calculation (2).  Conversely, the product transition-response law just constructed, together with the present joint external policy coins, completes an SCM attaining the same conditional mean-credit functional \(\Phi_i(q^{\mathrm{CI}})\).  These two observations are only a projection and completion statement for the transition component.  They assert no equivalence or inclusion of full SCM classes, no equality of joint counterfactual laws, and no conclusion about policy-response or reward mechanisms in the published scheme.

prose_overlay.tldr: For fixed ambient factual and baseline policies and a positive-probability factual trajectory, a finite Markov SCM with known deterministic transition rewards, independent transition disturbances across time, a complete joint external product of factual and coalition policy coins, and unrestricted within-time transition-response coupling yields an attained sharp interval for every trajectory-conditioned Shapley mean-credit coordinate.  Exact beta-integral compression reduces the \(2^H\) coalition sum to \(H\) Markov evaluations, and a legal mixed-elimination compiler returns both endpoints and compact compatible SCM witnesses in \(O(H^2Nd^{w_{\mathrm c}+1})\) rational operations.  A two-stage open family has shared interval \([-\varepsilon,\varepsilon/2]\), strictly inside the internal separate-coalition relaxation \([-(1+\varepsilon)/2,1/2]\).  An explicit row-product multinomial region gives simultaneous whole-set coverage, a finite boundary-aware endpoint algorithm, and endpoint error controlled by factual transition-cell positivity.
prose_overlay.related_work: Li, Lee, and Bareinboim (2026) define the trajectory intervention in a fuller counterfactual scheme.  At the transition component, their scheme projects to the same selected posterior \(q^{\mathrm{CI}}\); conversely, a product transition-response law together with this paper's joint external policy coins completes an SCM attaining the same conditional mean-credit functional.  This is component-level informed-by matching, not equivalence or inclusion of full SCM classes, joint counterfactual laws, policy-response mechanisms, or reward mechanisms.  Lee, Plecko, and Bareinboim (2026) optimize whole Layer-3 Shapley functionals over a generic neural-SCM family.  Lally, Kazemi, and Paoletti (2026) supply generic one-step row gluing; novelty here is confined to valid sequential trajectory conditioning, shared sequential Shapley optimization, exact compression and compilation, and confidence-fiber projection.  Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022), Choe et al. (2026), Arroyo et al. (2025), and Zaffalon et al. (2024) provide canonical-SCM, reduction, programming, and credal-network context.  Witter et al. (2026) motivate coalition compression but do not give this posterior shared-row endpoint.  Liu and Ihler (2013), Park and Darwiche (2004), and Choi, Friedman, and Van den Broeck (2022) provide marginal-MAP context; the legal-order invariant, common backpointer, sparse upper bound, and active-chain obstruction are proved directly here.  Hoeffding (1963) supplies the cellwise concentration inequality, while Wang (2008) studies exact multinomial simultaneous coefficients; the paper uses its own conservative union-bound product.  Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), Fang and Santos (2019), and Bennett et al. (2024) mark stronger inference rungs not claimed here.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: The exact compiler is exponential in the valid constrained width, not in ordinary temporal treewidth alone.  Sparse trajectories with \(|J|=O(\log H)\) and fixed alphabets give polynomial horizon cost, whereas fully active binary chains can force \(w_{\mathrm c}=\Omega(H)\).  Confidence-polytope vertex enumeration is finite and output-sensitive but no polynomial bound is claimed.  The paper does not provide root-normal inference, adaptive-sampling confidence sequences, or a jointly sharp box for all Shapley coordinates.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The causal class has finite state and action spaces, a fixed initial state, known deterministic transition rewards, independent transition disturbances across time, positive factual action and transition cells, and a complete finite product family of factual and coalition state-indexed response-function coins that is mutually independent and jointly independent of the initial state and transition disturbances.  The displayed \(\mathfrak M(K)\), its transition-independent subclass, and all \(\Theta_i\), \(L_i\), and \(U_i\) functionals suppress the fixed ambient \((\pi,\pi_{\mathrm{base}},\tau)\); policies are external mechanisms and never optimized.  Only coupling among potential next states for different state-action rows within a time is unrestricted.  The transition-component independence reduction neither equates nor orders full SCM classes and says nothing about published policy-response, reward-response, or joint-counterfactual mechanisms.  Population endpoints are attained.  Confidence endpoints use fixed rowwise multinomial sampling; zero-minimum blocks use closure values and positive-evidence approximating sequences, while a zero factual-cell maximum triggers only \([-D,D]\).  No sharp result is claimed for PTR's root-mean-square priority, exponential moving average, rankings, or learning performance.

Generic Layer-3 bounds do not expose finite Markov posterior rows, and one-step compatible-MDP gluing does not solve a signed Shapley objective over one transition SCM shared by all coalitions. sampling_model.overlap: Trajectory conditioning uses the sequentially derived positive action likelihood \(\prod_t\pi_t(a_t\mid s_t)>0\) and positive factual transition cells \(p_t=K_t(y_t\mid x_t)>0\).  Uniform endpoint stability uses the stronger transition bound \(p_t\ge\kappa\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each transition row is estimated by \(\widehat K_t(\cdot\mid x)\).  For positive counts the confidence row is the simplex intersected with the coordinate box of radius \(e_{t,x}\ge\sqrt{\log(2H|\mathcal X||\mathcal S|/\alpha)/(2n_{t,x})}\); confidence endpoints optimize the shared Shapley functional over the resulting closed posterior-row projection.
sampling_model.design: For each time-row, a fixed number of within-row independent multinomial next-state draws is observed.  Cross-row independence is not assumed: cellwise Hoeffding bounds are combined by a union bound into the explicit row-product region.  The factual and coalition policies are fixed external mechanisms, not sampled transition-model components, and adaptive online visitation is outside the theorem.
sampling_model.treatment: For every coalition, the known kernel \(\alpha_t^C\) is generated by its state-indexed response-function coins.  The complete family of factual and coalition coins is mutually independent and jointly independent of the initial state and transition disturbances; factual conditioning therefore leaves all coalition policy laws unchanged.  Sampling uncertainty concerns transition marginals only.
sampling_model.units: For row \((t,x)\), the units are the \(n_{t,x}\) observed next-state draws; a zero-count row contributes the full simplex.

prose_overlay.interpretation: The interval is the set of conditional mean credits compatible with the observed transition marginals, the fixed ambient policies and trajectory, and the stated transition-response SCM class.  One posterior transition-row assignment must serve every coalition world, while the complete external policy-coin family remains independent after factual conditioning.  If an interval excludes zero, the sign of that mean credit is robust to the unidentified transition-response coupling; if it crosses zero, the sign is not identified from these transition marginals.  The endpoint compiler returns a concrete compatible transition SCM and its canonical external policy-coin completion.  These statements concern the mean coordinate used by \(\phi\)-PPO, not PTR priority.
